reviewMethod: Manual browser inspection of public university-presented Vivid Media / Matterport tours using visible floorplan, dollhouse, floor selector, and interior controls. No private model or texture extraction.
credit: Presented by University of Richmond Residence Life & Housing; tour presentation © Vivid Media LLC; Matterport platform.
evidenceUse: Screenshots saved locally for research/reference only; not approved for republication. Link users to the provider tours.

tours.title: Gateway Apartment
visitedViews: Interior panorama; turned through sofa and kitchen/dining sightline
verifiedLayoutFeatures: Single-level example apartment with four distinct bedrooms, each showing one bed and desk/storage furniture.
A continuous shared living/dining/kitchen zone runs along the opposite side of the apartment from the bedrooms.
The kitchen has a range, refrigerator, cabinets, sink, and an island; a round dining table and chairs occupy the adjoining shared area.
An L-shaped sofa occupies the living end near windows.
Two centrally positioned enclosed bathroom compartments show toilets and bathing fixtures. Separate vanity/sink zones are visible toward the two bedroom-access sides.
Bedrooms are separated from the living space by walls and intervening bathroom/access areas; no bedroom is the only route between kitchen and living area.

layoutGraph.scope: Example apartment only; conceptual adjacency, no scale or compass orientation
layoutGraph.connectionNote: Left/right labels refer only to saved overhead view. Access routes are visually observed qualitative topology; exact door positions and swing geometry are not measured.

uncertainties: The scan shows one example unit/suite, not every layout or current assigned room in this hall.
No measurement was taken. Screenshots and adjacency notes are not calibrated geometry and must not be used to assign dimensions, floor area, ceiling height, or furniture clearance.
Tour furniture and finishes are visible at scan time; present inventory and permitted alterations were not verified.
Social atmosphere, noise transmission, demand, room eligibility, and meal-plan requirements cannot be established from this tour.
plannerQuizImplications: Score separate shared living space independently of bedroom area.
A preference for hosting while retaining a separate bedroom has visible physical support in this example.
Kitchen and dining furniture should be separate planner zones; keep the entry-to-bedroom circulation path free.
Do not represent the entire apartment as a large rectangular bedroom or combine its shared area into individual bedroom area.

tours.title: University Forest Apartment
verifiedLayoutFeatures: Two-level example apartment with an internal staircase connecting the shared lower level and bedroom upper level.
Lower floor has a separate living zone with L-shaped sofa and low tables, and a kitchen/dining zone with range, refrigerator, sink, cabinets, rectangular table, and chairs.
A small lower-level toilet-and-sink room sits beside the entrance/stair area.
Upper floor has two bedrooms, each showing two beds plus desks/storage.
A central upper bathroom zone sits between the bedrooms and shows toilet, bathing fixture, and sink.
Upper stair landing/corridor connects the two bedroom sides and shared bathroom; bedrooms are upstairs rather than in the lower living area.
A glazed exterior opening is visible at the living end.

layoutGraph.scope: Two-level example only; conceptual adjacency, no scale or compass orientation
layoutGraph.stairRelationship: Stair occupies the front/central boundary between living side and kitchen/dining side in saved lower-floor view; upper landing lies in the central corridor between bedroom sides. Exact stair footprint/direction is not calibrated.

uncertainties: The scan shows one example unit/suite, not every layout or current assigned room in this hall.
No measurement was taken. Screenshots and adjacency notes are not calibrated geometry and must not be used to assign dimensions, floor area, ceiling height, or furniture clearance.
Tour furniture and finishes are visible at scan time; present inventory and permitted alterations were not verified.
Social atmosphere, noise transmission, demand, room eligibility, and meal-plan requirements cannot be established from this tour.
plannerQuizImplications: Distinguish shared living downstairs from shared bedrooms upstairs; do not imply that UFA means a private bedroom.
A living-room preference and bedroom-sharing preference need separate quiz questions.
Support floor selection in planner and preserve stair/landing/bathroom zones as fixed circulation.
Use this tour as a two-level visual reference only, not proof that every UFA unit has this layout.

tours.title: Residence Hall #1 Single & Double with Suite Bath
verifiedLayoutFeatures: Example suite contains one double bedroom with two beds and one single bedroom with one bed.
A shared bathroom lies between the two bedrooms, with toilet, sink, and shower visible.
Bedroom footprints include window/dormer recesses; sloping ceiling planes are visible in the interior.
Desks, chairs, and wooden storage furniture are present; some beds are raised with storage beneath.
The scanned suite has no separate furnished living room or kitchen visible.

layoutGraph.connectionNote: Bathroom centrally joins suite bedrooms in overhead view; verify door swings against official plan before modeling.

uncertainties: The scan shows one example unit/suite, not every layout or current assigned room in this hall.
No measurement was taken. Screenshots and adjacency notes are not calibrated geometry and must not be used to assign dimensions, floor area, ceiling height, or furniture clearance.
Tour furniture and finishes are visible at scan time; present inventory and permitted alterations were not verified.
Social atmosphere, noise transmission, demand, room eligibility, and meal-plan requirements cannot be established from this tour.
The tour title specifies single and double with suite bath. It does not establish the proportion of these room types throughout the hall.
plannerQuizImplications: Offer single versus double room choices within this hall, rather than a single hall-level bedroom assumption.
Retain dormer recesses in room outlines; flat floor area alone does not describe sloped-ceiling usability.
Do not invent a separate suite lounge or score apartment-style hosting space from the word suite.

tours.title: Residence Hall #2 Single/Double Suite
verifiedLayoutFeatures: Example suite has one single bedroom and one double bedroom; three beds are visible in total.
A central connecting vestibule/vanity area has two sinks and connects the bedroom sides.
An enclosed central bathroom compartment contains toilet and shower, separate from the visible vanity area.
The single bedroom is narrower than the double in the saved overhead view, without any measured dimensions.
Beds, desks, chairs, dressers, and closet/storage areas are visible.
No separate furnished living room or kitchen is visible within this scanned suite.
uncertainties: The scan shows one example unit/suite, not every layout or current assigned room in this hall.
No measurement was taken. Screenshots and adjacency notes are not calibrated geometry and must not be used to assign dimensions, floor area, ceiling height, or furniture clearance.
Tour furniture and finishes are visible at scan time; present inventory and permitted alterations were not verified.
Social atmosphere, noise transmission, demand, room eligibility, and meal-plan requirements cannot be established from this tour.
plannerQuizImplications: Bathroom arrangement can be described more precisely than simply suite bath: vanity and toilet/shower areas are separated in this example.
Quiz should distinguish bedroom sharing from bathroom sharing.
Keep vestibule and bath circulation clear in room planner; do not count this passage as a lounge.

No separate furnished living room or kitchen is visible in this scan.
